name: Sobel Magnitude Distribution
algorithm: Sobel Magnitude Distribution — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes Sobel magnitude distributions for image forensic analysis following Sobel & Feldman (1968):

1. **Sobel Edge Detection**: The Sobel operator computes horizontal (Gx) and vertical (Gy) gradients using 3×3 kernels. The gradient magnitude G = √(Gx² + Gy²) and direction θ = arctan(Gy/Gx) are computed at each pixel, providing a robust measure of edge strength and orientation.

2. **Magnitude Distribution Analysis**: The histogram of Sobel magnitude values across the image is analyzed. Natural images show specific magnitude distributions following approximately an exponential or Weibull distribution. AI-generated images may show different distributions — modified tail behavior, unusual peak structures, or distribution shape inconsistent with optical imaging.

3. **Spatial Magnitude Patterns**: The spatial distribution of Sobel magnitudes reveals the image's edge structure. In natural images, high-magnitude pixels (strong edges) form connected contours following object boundaries. AI-generated images may show: fragmented edge structures, edge magnitudes not consistent with depth-of-field expectations, or unnaturally uniform edge strength.

4. **Magnitude-Direction Correlation**: In natural images, edge magnitude and direction are correlated through scene structure — strong edges along object boundaries have coherent directions. The method analyzes magnitude-direction correlation. AI artifacts may produce strong gradients with incoherent directions.

5. **Sobel Feature Scoring**: Sobel magnitude features (distribution parameters, spatial patterns, magnitude-direction correlation, multi-scale behavior) are combined into a forensic score. The score measures deviation from natural image edge statistics.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through sobel magnitude distribution analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used

Gonzalez, R.C. & Woods, R.E. (2018). Digital Image Processing. 4th Edition. Pearson.
